title: Microsoft breaks Patch Tuesday's monthly cadence for AI-surface fixes by Q2 2027
body: Microsoft will split its AI surfaces out of the monthly Patch Tuesday rhythm and ship them on a faster-than-monthly security servicing cadence. The July 14 release fixed a record 570 vulnerabilities, and the striking part was not just the volume but the composition: a critical remote-code-execution flaw in Microsoft Copilot itself (CVE-2026-48561), a GitHub Copilot RCE, a Copilot/VS Code security-feature bypass, and a Copilot/VS Code token-disclosure flaw — the assistant and its host editor now form a recurring vulnerability category rather than an exotic one-off. Microsoft attributes the record volume to its own AI-powered internal vulnerability-discovery system, which means the pipeline producing these findings will keep accelerating, and Adobe responded to the same pressure the same day by moving to twice-monthly bulletins, citing AI-accelerated discovery compressing the window between disclosure and exploitation. A monthly batch cycle designed for operating-system components sits badly on cloud-updated assistants whose flaws are found continuously and weaponized quickly; Copilot fixes largely deploy server-side anyway, so the engineering cost of decoupling them is low while the exposure cost of holding them for a monthly train keeps rising. The prediction is that Microsoft formalizes this: either a publicly documented accelerated cadence for Copilot-class services or a dedicated AI-surface security servicing channel, announced by Q2 2027.

reasoning.given: AI-assisted discovery compresses disclosure-to-exploit windows; Adobe already moved to twice-monthly
reasoning.so_that: Microsoft ships a faster-than-monthly security servicing channel for Copilot and other AI surfaces
reasoning.landing: by Q2 2027; Microsoft announces faster-than-monthly Copilot security cadence
reasoning.plain_language: Hackers and defenders both use AI to find bugs faster, so Microsoft will start shipping Copilot security fixes more often than once a month.

summary: Copilot and VS Code flaws are now a recurring Patch Tuesday category, and AI-assisted discovery is inflating CVE volume while shrinking exploit windows. Adobe already went twice-monthly. Microsoft follows by Q2 2027 with a faster-than-monthly security cadence for its AI surfaces.
